newsitem.title: CHINA: Singapore Telecom signs China GSM deal.
newsitem.headline: Singapore Telecom signs China GSM deal.

text.p: Singapore Telecom MobileLink Pte Ltd has signed an agreement with China Telecom to provide roaming service for mobile telephone users travelling between the two countries, the China Daily said on Thursday.

The new service would allow Chinese and Singaporean subscribers to the Global System for Mobile Communications (GSM) to operate cellular telephone services during visits to China and Singapore, the newspaper said.
Singapore Telecom MobileLink is a unit of Singapore Telecommunications Ltd while China Telecom is an operating unit of China's Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications.
Travellers made over 500,000 trips between China and Singapore in 1995, and that figure was expected to grow by 30 percent a year, the official newspaper said.
China Telecom set up roaming service links with Hong Kong Telecom CSL in July and would sign a roaming service deal with Finland next, it said, adding similar pacts were planned with other countries.
China had 5.6 million cellular phone subscribers as of August, including 890,000 GSM subscribers, the China Daily said, citing telecommunications ministry statistics.
Beijing now had more than 100,000 GSM subscribers and the city was working on a project to boost network capacity to more than 250,000 users by the end of 1996, it said.
GSM service was available in 15 provinces, regions and municipalities in China by the start of this year, it said.
